mainTopic: The שבועות offerings and the שתי הלחם: which ones hold each other up, the מחלוקת of רבי עקיבא and בן ננס about the two sheep, and the פסוקים each side learns from.
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier teaching: if there is not enough flour for all the rams, bring one ram with its flour rather than all of them without it. A new משנה then teaches that the main שבועות offerings and the שתי הלחם do not hold each other up. About the two sheep brought with the לחם, רבי עקיבא says the לחם holds up the sheep, while רבי שמעון בן ננס says the reverse and points to the מדבר. רבי שמעון agrees with בן ננס's ruling but rejects his proof: the sheep permit themselves, while the bread needs the sheep to permit it. The גמרא brings a ברייתא with רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא on the verse 'על הלחם', and shows that the offering lists in ויקרא and במדבר are separate groups. It then gives the sources for רבי עקיבא and בן ננס: competing גזירה שוה links (יהיו to תהיינה, or יהיו to יהיו), or two readings of 'קדש יהיו לה׳ לכהן'. The amud ends as רבי יוחנן begins a point that everyone agrees on, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Many rams but not enough flour: bring one ram properly
steps.stepSummary: The closing ruling of an earlier teaching. If there are many rams to offer but not enough flour for all their flour offerings, bring one ram with its flour. Do not bring all the rams without flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there were many rams and they did not have the flour offerings for them, they should bring one ram with its flour, and not offer all of them without flour.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a teaching that started before this section. It answers what to do when there is not enough flour for every ram's accompanying offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule picks quality over quantity. One ram brought the complete, correct way is better than many rams each missing its required flour offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Rams
A measure of flour; here it means the flour offering that goes with each animal
They should be offered (on the מזבח)

steps.whatToRemember: Better one ram done completely than many rams done incompletely.

phrases.aramaic: אֵילִים מְרוּבִּין וְלֹא הָיָה לָהֶן אֵיפָתָן –
phrases.english: If there were many rams and they did not have their ephahs of flour,
phrases.notes: 'Ephah' here just means the flour offering that each ram needs.

phrases.english: they should bring one ram and its ephah,
and they should not offer all of them without ephahs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵילִים מְרוּבִּין וְלֹא הָיָה לָהֶן אֵיפָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a teaching that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: When the flour is limited, bring one complete ram with its flour rather than many rams without it.

steps.title: The animal offerings and the bread do not hold each other up
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. The bull, the rams, the sheep and the goat of שבועות do not hold up the שתי הלחם, and the לחם does not hold them up.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The bull, the rams, the sheep and the goat do not hold up the bread, and the bread does not hold them up.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It says that each group of שבועות offerings can be brought even if the other group is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something that is מעכב must be present for the other thing to be valid. Here the משנה says the main animal offerings and the שתי הלחם are independent of each other. If one is missing, the other is still brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Hold up / prevent: without this, the other cannot be brought
Bull
Goat, brought as a חטאת
The two loaves of שבועות

steps.confusionAlert: The 'sheep' in this line are the seven sheep brought as עולות. They are not the two sheep waved with the bread, which are discussed in the next line.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The bull, the rams, the sheep, and the goat
do not prevent the bread,
and the bread does not prevent them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפָּר וְהָאֵילִים וְהַכְּבָשִׂים וְהַשָּׂעִיר אֵין מְעַכְּבִין אֶת הַלֶּחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on the offerings of שבועות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bull, the rams, the seven sheep and the goat, and the שתי הלחם, do not hold each other up.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the bread holds up the two sheep
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rules that without the לחם, the two accompanying sheep cannot be brought. But without the sheep, the לחם can still be brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bread holds up the sheep, but the sheep do not hold up the bread. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns to the two sheep brought as שלמים together with the לחם. רבי עקיבא says the bread is the essential part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the dependence goes one way only. For רבי עקיבא the sheep need the לחם, but the לחם does not need the sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: Sheep; here, the two sheep of שלמים waved with the bread
Holds up (singular form)

phrases.english: The bread prevents the sheep,
phrases.notes: These are the two sheep brought as שלמים together with the bread, not the seven from the line before.

phrases.english: but the sheep do not prevent the bread;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַלֶּחֶם מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַכְּבָשִׂים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the main offerings to the two sheep that go with the bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא: the לחם is required for the sheep; the sheep are not required for the לחם.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן ננס: the opposite, the sheep hold up the bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן ננס disagrees and flips רבי עקיבא's ruling. The sheep are required for the לחם, but the לחם is not required for the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן ננס said: Not so. Rather, the sheep hold up the bread, and the bread does not hold up the sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא argues and states the exact reverse of רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that the dependence goes in one direction only. They argue about which item is the main one: רבי עקיבא says the לחם, רבי שמעון בן ננס says the sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: Not so: an opening that rejects the previous view
Rather

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס: לֹא כִּי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Nannas said: Not so,
rather the sheep prevent the bread,
and the bread does not prevent the sheep,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן נַנָּס לֹא כִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי עקיבא and reverses his ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון בן ננס: the sheep are required for the לחם; the לחם is not required for the sheep.

steps.title: Proof from the forty years in the desert
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן ננס proves his view. In the מדבר, the sheep were offered without לחם, so today too the sheep may be offered without לחם.
steps.simpleTranslation: For we found that when ישראל were in the desert forty years, sheep were offered without bread. So here too, sheep may be offered without bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן ננס backs up his ruling with a proof from history.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sheep were offered in the מדבר without any לחם, then the לחם cannot be a requirement for the sheep. That supports the half of his ruling that says the לחם does not hold up the sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: For so we have found: introduces a proof from an earlier case
The desert, where ישראל spent forty years
Here too: applies the earlier case to the present one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: the לחם is the main item. רבי שמעון בן ננס: the sheep are the main item, as the מדבר shows.

phrases.english: for so we have found that when the Jewish people were
in the desert for forty years,
sheep were offered without bread,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן יִקְרְבוּ כְּבָשִׂים בְּלֹא לֶחֶם.
phrases.english: so here too, sheep may be offered without bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ כְּשֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמִדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רבי שמעון בן ננס's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That the לחם does not hold up the sheep
steps.raayaSupportSource: The forty years in the מדבר, when sheep were offered without לחם

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees with the ruling but not the reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says the הלכה follows בן ננס, but the reason בן ננס gave is wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said: The law follows בן ננס, but his reason is not correct.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion, רבי שמעון, enters. He accepts בן ננס's bottom line but announces that he will reject the reasoning behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This splits the ruling from the reason. In practice, the כבשים can be brought without the לחם, but not the other way around. The proof from the מדבר (Step 5) is about to be knocked down and replaced.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law we follow
The reason behind a ruling

steps.confusionAlert: Agreeing with a ruling does not mean agreeing with its proof. רבי שמעון rules like בן ננס but for a totally different reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said:
The law is like the words of ben Nannas,
phrases.notes: He means רבי שמעון בן ננס from Step 4: the sheep can come without the bread, but not the reverse.

phrases.english: but the reason is not like his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי בֶּן נַנָּס, אֲבָל אֵין הַטַּעַם כִּדְבָרָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the ruling of Step 4 while preparing to reject the proof of Step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows בן ננס's ruling, but not his reasoning.

steps.title: The proof from the wilderness fails
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון explains that the לחם's offerings were never brought in the מדבר. Both groups of offerings began only in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offerings listed in the book of במדבר were brought in the מדבר. The offerings listed in ויקרא were not brought in the מדבר. Once they came into the land, both groups were brought.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון knocks down בן ננס's proof. In the מדבר, the sheep were never brought without the bread, because the bread's offerings were not brought there at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן ננס assumed that the sheep were brought in the מדבר while the bread was not. רבי שמעון says the sheep belong to the ויקרא list, which only started in ארץ ישראל together with the bread. So the מדבר gives no example of sheep brought without bread.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of the countings, meaning ספר במדבר
The law of the כהנים, meaning ספר ויקרא
Was offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: For everything stated in the book of the countings
phrases.notes: This is ספר במדבר, named after its counting of the people. Its שבועות offerings are in במדבר 28:27.

phrases.english: was offered in the wilderness,
and everything stated in the law of the priests
phrases.notes: This is ספר ויקרא. The offerings that come with the bread are listed in ויקרא 23:18–20.

phrases.english: was not offered in the wilderness,
once they came to the land,
these and those were offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכׇּל הָאָמוּר בְּחוֹמֶשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים קָרֵב בַּמִּדְבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the reason in Step 6 is rejected by taking apart the proof from Step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only בן ננס's proof from the מדבר, not his ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sheep and their bread both belong to the ויקרא list, which was not brought at all in the מדבר. So the מדבר never showed sheep brought without bread.

steps.title: The real reason: the sheep permit themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's own reason is that the כבשים make themselves permitted, while the לחם needs the כבשים to permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I say the sheep can be brought without the bread? Because the sheep permit themselves. But the bread cannot be brought without the sheep, because it has nothing else to permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected בן ננס's proof, רבי שמעון now gives his own reason for the same ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offering the sheep on the מזבח makes their own meat permitted, so they do not need the bread. The bread, however, only becomes permitted through the sheep. So the bread cannot stand alone, but the sheep can.

keyTerms.meaning: They make themselves permitted
Will make it permitted

steps.whatToRemember: The final ruling of the משנה: the sheep can be brought without the bread, but the bread cannot be brought without the sheep. The reason is that the sheep permit themselves and the bread depends on the sheep.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule in a clear idea: whatever has no other way to become permitted depends on the item that permits it.

phrases.english: For what reason do I say
that the sheep should be offered without bread?
Because the sheep permit themselves,
phrases.notes: Bringing the sheep on the מזבח is what lets their own meat be eaten, so they need nothing else.

phrases.english: and not the bread without the sheep —
for it has nothing that will permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִפְּנֵי מָה אֲנִי אוֹמֵר יִקְרְבוּ כְּבָשִׂים בְּלֹא לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of Step 7 with a new reason for the same ruling
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the sheep may be offered without the bread, but not the bread without the sheep
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: the sheep permit themselves, while the bread is permitted only through the sheep

steps.title: A ברייתא reads the verse about the bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא. One part of the פסוק ties the offerings to the bread, but the seven lambs may be brought even without bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: 'And you shall offer with the bread' teaches that these offerings depend on the bread. 'Seven unblemished lambs' teaches that they are brought even if there is no bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא section begins. It brings a ברייתא that splits the פסוק into two parts to show which offerings depend on the bread and which do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'with the bread' make the offerings listed there an obligation tied to the bread. The words 'seven unblemished lambs' teach that the lambs come even when there is no bread. So one פסוק carries both a dependence and an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that follows the משנה
An obligation tied to the bread
Without blemish
Even though there is no

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
"And you shall offer with the bread" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:18

phrases.english: it is an obligation tied to the bread,
"seven unblemished lambs" —
even though there is no bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְהִקְרַבְתֶּם עַל הַלֶּחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by bringing a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about the offerings that come with the bread
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'With the bread' makes the offerings an obligation tied to the bread, while 'seven unblemished lambs' teaches that the lambs are brought even without bread.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say 'with the bread'?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: if the sheep may be brought without bread, what do the words "על הלחם" teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse teach by saying "with the bread"?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question about its own ruling. This sets up the next step, where רבי טרפון explains the words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the seven lambs may be brought even without the bread. But the פסוק links them to the bread with the words "על הלחם". So those words must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what we just said is true
What does the verse come to teach by saying this?
With the bread (the שתי הלחם of שבועות)

phrases.english: If so,
what does the verse teach by saying "with the bread"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:18

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the words "על הלחם" mean, given the ruling in Step 9 that the lambs do not need the bread.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words "על הלחם" teach, if they do not make the sheep depend on the bread.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: the sheep obligation began with the bread obligation
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון says the words teach timing: the sheep became required only when the bread became required.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that they were not obligated to bring the sheep before they were obligated to bring the bread. These are the words of רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון answers the question. "על הלחם" tells us when the sheep became required, not that each sacrifice needs the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link to the bread is about the start date of the obligation. Both obligations began together, in ארץ ישראל. Once that obligation exists, the sheep can still be offered even if there is no bread.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches
They became obligated
Sheep or lambs

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי טרפון, "על הלחם" is about when the obligation started, not a rule that each offering needs the bread.

phrases.english: It teaches that they were not obligated in the sheep
before they were obligated in the bread,
these are the words of Rabbi Tarfon.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְחַיְּיבוּ בַּכְּבָשִׂים קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּתְחַיְּיבוּ בַּלֶּחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "על הלחם" teaches that the sheep obligation began at the same time as the bread obligation.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the two lists describe different offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא proves that the sheep in ויקרא are not the sheep in במדבר. The bulls and rams do not match, so the lists are separate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: You might think the sheep mentioned here are the very same sheep mentioned in the book of במדבר. But when you reach the bulls and rams, you must say they are not the same. Rather, these come for their own sake, and those come for the sake of the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא offers a different approach. He shows that the תורה lists two separate groups of offerings for שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The numbers of bulls and rams in ויקרא and in במדבר do not match, so the two lists cannot be the same offerings. That means there are two sets. One set (במדבר) is brought for itself, and the other set (ויקרא) is brought because of the לחם.

keyTerms.meaning: One might have thought
The book of במדבר
Bulls and rams
Because of; for the sake of

steps.confusionAlert: Both lists belong to שבועות, which makes it easy to assume they are one group. רבי עקיבא's whole point is that they are two separate groups.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל הֵן הֵן כְּבָשִׂים הָאֲמוּרִים כָּאן
phrases.english: One might think the sheep mentioned here

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן כְּבָשִׂים הָאֲמוּרִים בְּחוֹמֶשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים?
phrases.english: are the very same sheep mentioned in the book of Numbers?
phrases.notes: "Here" means ספר ויקרא. The list in Numbers is the מוספין of שבועות, במדבר 28:27.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַרְתָּ, כְּשֶׁאַתָּה מַגִּיעַ אֵצֶל פָּרִים וְאֵילִים
phrases.english: You must say, when you reach the bulls and rams,
they are not the same ones,
rather, these come for their own sake,
and those come for the sake of the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: יָכוֹל הֵן הֵן כְּבָשִׂים הָאֲמוּרִים כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different view from רבי טרפון's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offerings in ויקרא (brought for the לחם) are separate from the מוספין in במדבר (brought for their own sake).

steps.title: Result: only the במדבר offerings were brought in the wilderness
steps.stepSummary: Because the lists are separate, the מוספין were offered in the מדבר, but the offerings that come with the bread were not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that what is said in the book of במדבר was offered in the wilderness, and what is said in ויקרא was not offered in the wilderness.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא draws the practical result of his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ויקרא offerings come because of the לחם. The לחם was not brought in the מדבר, so those offerings were not brought there either. The מוספין stand on their own, so they were offered.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out; the result is
The book of ויקרא
Was offered

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא: the במדבר offerings stand on their own and were brought in the מדבר. The ויקרא offerings depend on the לחם and were not.

phrases.english: It turns out, what is said in the book of Numbers
was offered in the wilderness,
and what is said in Leviticus
was not offered in the wilderness.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא, מַה שֶּׁאָמוּר בְּחוֹמֶשׁ הַפְּקוּדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of רבי עקיבא's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מוספין of במדבר were offered in the מדבר. The offerings of ויקרא were not.

steps.title: Maybe only the sheep are shared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: the bulls and rams may be different, but the sheep might still be the same in both lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the bulls and rams are not the same, yet the sheep are the very same ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי עקיבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mismatch only shows that the bulls and rams are different. Both lists have seven sheep, so those could still be one group counted in both places.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
They are the very same ones

phrases.english: But perhaps the bulls and rams are not the same,
yet the sheep are the very same ones?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא פָּרִים וְאֵילִים לָאו אִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's proof that the two lists are completely separate.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A difference in the bulls and rams does not prove a difference in the sheep.

steps.title: If part of the list differs, the whole list differs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: since the bulls and rams differ, the sheep must also be a separate group.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since these were changed, these too are other ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי עקיבא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each list is one group of offerings. Once we know the bulls and rams are separate, the sheep in that same list are separate as well. So רבי עקיבא's conclusion stands.

keyTerms.meaning: They were changed; they are different
Other ones; different ones

steps.whatToRemember: The two lists are fully separate, sheep included. So the sheep that come with the לחם were not brought in the מדבר.

phrases.english: Since these were changed,
phrases.notes: "These" means the bulls and rams.

phrases.english: these too are other ones.
phrases.notes: "These" now means the sheep.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּהָנֵי אִישְׁתַּנּוֹ, הָנֵי נָמֵי דְּאַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical inference from the parts of the list to the whole list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sheep might be shared between the two lists.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the bulls and rams differ, the sheep are separate too.

steps.title: Maybe the bulls and rams are one offering with a choice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the bulls and rams in the two lists are different. Maybe the תורה is just letting you choose one of two combinations.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know the bulls and rams are different offerings? Maybe the תורה means: if you want, bring one bull and two rams; if you want, bring two bulls and one ram.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the very starting point of רבי עקיבא's proof: that the bulls and rams in the two lists are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 15, the גמרא used the bulls and rams to prove the sheep are separate too. Now it asks whether the bulls and rams are even different offerings. Maybe ויקרא and במדבר describe one single offering, with a choice between two combinations. If so, the whole proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? How do we know?
They are different, changed
Perhaps, maybe
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
If he wants, giving a choice

phrases.english: And the bulls and rams, from where do we know that they are different?
Perhaps this is what the Merciful One is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי פַּר וּשְׁנֵי אֵילִים לִיקְרַב,
phrases.english: If one wants, let him offer a bull and two rams,
phrases.notes: This is the list in ויקרא 23:18.

phrases.aramaic: אִי בָּעֵי שְׁנֵי פָּרִים וְאַיִל אֶחָד לִיקְרַב!
phrases.english: if one wants, let him offer two bulls and one ram!
phrases.notes: This is the list in במדבר 28:27.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפָרִים וְאֵילִים, מִמַּאי דְּאִישְׁתַּנּוֹ? דִּלְמָא הָכִי קָאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption that Step 15's answer was built on: that the bulls and rams really differ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the bulls and rams in ויקרא and במדבר are different offerings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two lists could describe one offering with a choice of two combinations, so their difference proves nothing about separate sets.

steps.title: The different order proves they are separate offerings
steps.stepSummary: The two lists are written in a different order, so they must be two separate sets of offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the order of the offerings is different in the two places, learn from this that they are separate offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The two lists put the animals in a different order, so they are two separate offerings, not one offering with a choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה only meant to give a choice, it would list the animals in the same order. ויקרא lists sheep, bull, rams, while במדבר lists bulls, ram, sheep. The changed order shows these are two different groups. That brings back רבי עקיבא's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Their order
Learn from it, conclude from this
They are other ones, separate items

steps.whatToRemember: The two lists in ויקרא and במדבר are separate offerings. So the מוספין of במדבר are not the offerings that come with the bread.

phrases.english: From the fact that their order is different,
learn from it that they are different offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאִישְׁתַּנִּי סִדְרָן, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 16's challenge and protects רבי עקיבא's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual proof from the order of the פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two lists might be one offering with a choice of combinations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The change in order shows they are two separate sets of offerings.

steps.title: Why does the bread hold back the sheep
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the bread holds back the sheep and asks for רבי עקיבא's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bread holds back the sheep. What is רבי עקיבא's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks where רבי עקיבא gets this rule, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that without the שתי הלחם, the two כבשים cannot be offered. But without the sheep, the bread can still be brought. The גמרא wants the source that makes the bread, and not the sheep, the essential part.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back; without it, the other thing cannot be done
Sheep, here the two sheep brought with the bread
What is the reason?

steps.confusionAlert: Read the direction carefully. Missing bread stops the sheep. Missing sheep does NOT stop the bread.

phrases.english: The bread holds back the sheep,
what is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of separate lists back to another ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי עקיבא's rule that the bread holds back the sheep

steps.title: A word link shows the bread is essential
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא learns from a גזירה שוה between יהיו and תהיינה that the essential item is the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns the word 'they shall be' (יהיו) from 'they shall be' (תהיינה). Just as there it is about the bread, so too here it is about the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. It links two similar words to show that the essential, must-have item is the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יהיו (ויקרא 23:20) teaches that something is essential, but it is unclear whether it means the bread or the sheep. The similar word תהיינה (ויקרא 23:17) clearly speaks about the bread. So יהיו also refers to the bread. That is why missing bread stops the sheep, but missing sheep does not stop the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: He learned, derived, here through a גְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה (a link between similar words)
'They shall be', which shows that something is essential
Just as there... so too here, the pattern of a word link

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, the bread is the essential part. The sheep depend on the bread, not the other way around.

phrases.english: He derived 'they shall be' from 'they shall be.'
phrases.notes: יהיו is in ויקרא 23:20, and תהיינה is in ויקרא 23:17.

phrases.english: Just as there it is the bread,
so too here it is the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר ״יִהְיוּ״ מִ״תִּהְיֶינָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה between יהיו and תהיינה shows that the essential element is the bread, so the bread holds back the sheep.

steps.title: בן ננס learns from the matching word יהיו that the sheep are essential
steps.stepSummary: בן ננס links the word יהיו in our פסוק to יהיו said about the seven sheep, so the essential item here is the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בן ננס? He learned it from 'יהיו' and 'יהיו': just as there it is talking about sheep, so too here it is talking about sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after giving רבי עקיבא's source, the גמרא now gives the source for the opposite view of בן ננס. He uses a גזירה שוה from the same word, יהיו, which points to the sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our פסוק about the שבועות offering says 'קדש יהיו', and another פסוק about the seven sheep says 'יהיו עלה'. Because the same word appears in both, בן ננס says the 'must be' requirement here is about the sheep, not the bread. So for him, missing sheep hold back the bread, but missing bread does not hold back the sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: he learned / derived (from another פסוק)
just as there... so too here (the standard form of a גזירה שוה)
sheep (lambs) brought as offerings

phrases.english: And בן ננס, how does he learn it?
he learned 'they shall be' from 'they shall be'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:20 and ויקרא 23:18

phrases.english: just as there it is sheep,
so too here it is sheep.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֶן נַנָּס, גָּמַר ״יִהְיוּ״ ״יִהְיוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 19: after רבי עקיבא's source, the גמרא gives the source for the other opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is בן ננס's source that the sheep are the essential item?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה between יהיו here and יהיו by the seven sheep, so the sheep are essential.

steps.title: Why doesn't בן ננס also learn from תהיינה, which points to the bread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בן ננס: the link to תהיינה used by רבי עקיבא is also available, and it points to the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בן ננס too should learn from 'תהיינה': just as there it is bread, so too here it is bread!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בן ננס. Why does he ignore רבי עקיבא's link, which would make the bread the essential item?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two possible links exist: יהיו to יהיו (sheep) and יהיו to תהיינה (bread). The question is why בן ננס picks the first one and not the second.

keyTerms.meaning: let us learn / derive
'they shall be' (feminine form), said about the loaves
bread (here, the two loaves of שבועות)

phrases.english: And בן ננס too
should learn from 'they shall be' (feminine form),
just as there it is bread,
so too here it is bread?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֶן נַנָּס נָמֵי נֵילַף מִ״תִּהְיֶינָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source just given for בן ננס in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: בן ננס's choice of the יהיו–יהיו link
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The יהיו–תהיינה link is also available and would make the bread essential, so why not use it?

steps.title: An identical word makes a better link than a similar word
steps.stepSummary: We link יהיו to the same word יהיו, not to the slightly different word תהיינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn 'יהיו' from 'יהיו', and we do not learn 'יהיו' from 'תהיינה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בן ננס prefers an exact word match. A link between two identical words is stronger than a link between two similar words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהיו and תהיינה come from the same root but are different forms. When an exact match exists, it is the better source for a גזירה שוה.

keyTerms.meaning: we learn / derive (one thing from another)
and we do not learn

phrases.english: We learn 'they shall be' from 'they shall be',
and we do not learn 'they shall be' from 'they shall be' (feminine form).

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין ״יִהְיוּ״ מִ״יִּהְיוּ״, וְאֵין דָּנִין ״יִהְיוּ״ מִ״תִּהְיֶינָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranking of sources: an identical word beats a similar word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both links seem equally valid, so בן ננס should agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The identical-word link (to the sheep) is preferred.

steps.title: Challenge from דבי רבי ישמעאל, who links two different words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why an exact match matters, since דבי רבי ישמעאל link שיבה and ביאה, which are completely different words.
steps.simpleTranslation: What difference does it make? Didn't the school of רבי ישמעאל teach: 'And the כהן shall return' and 'And the כהן shall come': this returning is the same as this coming.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 22. דבי רבי ישמעאל made a גזירה שוה between two totally different words, so exact matching does not seem to matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the laws of נגעי בתים, דבי רבי ישמעאל compare 'ושב הכהן' with 'ובא הכהן', even though the words share nothing. If such different words can be linked, then יהיו and תהיינה, which are almost the same, should be a perfectly good link too.

keyTerms.meaning: what difference does it make?
returning (from 'וְשָׁב הַכֹּהֵן')
coming (from 'וּבָא הַכֹּהֵן')

phrases.english: What difference does it make?
phrases.notes: He means: why should it matter whether the two words are exactly the same?

phrases.english: But didn't the school of רבי ישמעאל teach:
'And the כהן shall return' and 'And the כהן shall come':
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:39 and ויקרא 14:44, about a house with a נגע.

phrases.english: this is returning, this is coming.
phrases.notes: Returning and coming are treated as the same thing, so the law of one applies to the other.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ? הָתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule given in step 22 that an identical word is required or preferred.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that an identical word beats a similar word
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even completely different words (שיבה/ביאה) can make a גזירה שוה, then the near-identical יהיו/תהיינה should work too.

steps.title: Similar words are used only when no identical word is available
steps.stepSummary: Linking different words, like שיבה and ביאה, is allowed only when there is no identical word. When an identical word exists, we learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only where there is nothing identical to it. But where there is something identical to it, we learn from what is identical to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. דבי רבי ישמעאל used different words only because nothing better was available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A similar-word link is valid, but it is a fallback. Here the identical word יהיו exists, so בן ננס learns from it, and the sheep are the essential item for him.

keyTerms.meaning: this applies only (when...)
that is identical to it / matches it
we learn / derive

steps.whatToRemember: A גזירה שוה can link similar words (like שיבה and ביאה), but an identical word always comes first. That is why בן ננס learns יהיו from יהיו (sheep) and not from תהיינה (bread).

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: This applies only where there is nothing identical to it,
but where there is something identical to it,
we learn from what is identical to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּדָמֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23 and confirms the answer of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since different words can be linked, יהיו/תהיינה is just as good as יהיו/יהיו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Different words are linked only when no identical word exists. When one exists, it takes priority.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי עקיבא also use the exact-match link?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא does not link יהיו to the identical word יהיו, as בן ננס does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let רבי עקיבא also learn the word יהיו from the identical word יהיו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question around and challenges רבי עקיבא. We just said an identical word is the better link, so why doesn't he use it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 24 we decided that when an identical word exists, we learn from it. The seven sheep are described with the identical word יהיו. So רבי עקיבא's link to תהיינה (the bread) now seems weaker, and the גמרא asks him to explain.

keyTerms.meaning: let him learn / derive
"they shall be": the key word in the פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva too
let him derive "yihyu" from "yihyu"!
phrases.notes: The second יהיו is the word used about the seven sheep, the link בן ננס used in Step 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נָמֵי לֵילַף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from Step 24 against רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's link of יהיו to תהיינה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an identical word is preferred, רבי עקיבא should link to the identical יהיו of the sheep.

steps.title: Learn a gift to the כהן from a gift to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא prefers a link based on content: the loaves are a gift to the כהן, like our case. The seven sheep are עולות and are not a gift to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: We derive something that is a gift to the כהן from something that is a gift to the כהן. This excludes those seven sheep, which are עולות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי עקיבא. A closer match in subject matters more to him than an exact match in wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our פסוק talks about items given to the כהן. The two loaves (the תהיינה פסוק) also go to the כהן, but the seven sheep are burned completely on the מזבח as עולות. So for רבי עקיבא, matching the subject beats matching the exact word.

keyTerms.meaning: we derive / learn (one case from another)
a gift given to the כהן
to exclude
burnt offerings, burned entirely on the מזבח

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two ways to choose between links: by identical wording (בן ננס) or by similar subject matter (רבי עקיבא).

phrases.english: We derive an item that is a gift to the priest
from an item that is a gift to the priest,
phrases.notes: This means the two loaves, which the כהן receives (ויקרא 23:17).

phrases.english: to exclude these, which are burnt offerings.
phrases.notes: "These" are the seven sheep of ויקרא 23:18.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּנִין דָּבָר שֶׁמַּתָּנָה לַכֹּהֵן מִדָּבָר שֶׁמַּתָּנָה לַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Matching by subject matter outweighs matching by identical wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא should prefer the identical word יהיו (the sheep)
steps.terutzMaskana: He prefers the link to the bread because both are gifts to the כהן, while the seven sheep are עולות
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא links by subject (gift to the כהן → the bread). בן ננס links by identical word (יהיו → the sheep).

steps.title: Second explanation: they read the פסוק itself differently, and רבי עקיבא says bread
steps.stepSummary: Alternatively, the argument comes from the phrase "holy to ה׳ for the כהן." רבי עקיבא says the item given wholly to the כהן is the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say they disagree about the פסוק itself: "They shall be holy to ה׳ for the כהן." רבי עקיבא holds: which item goes entirely to the כהן? The bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a completely different explanation of the argument. It is not about word links at all; it is about how to read our פסוק. This step gives רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "For the כהן" points to something that belongs fully to the כהן. The two loaves are eaten entirely by the כהנים, so יהיו refers to the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you wish, say: introduces another explanation
about the פסוק itself
they disagree
that is entirely for the כהן

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
they disagree about the verse itself:
"They shall be holy to the Lord for the priest."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:20

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
Which item is entirely for the priest?
You must say: this is the bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, בִּקְרָא גּוּפֵיהּ קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different basis for the whole argument instead of the word links
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative explanation of the source of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument depends on which word link to use
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument may come from reading "לה׳ לכהן" itself; רבי עקיבא reads it as wholly for the כהן, meaning the bread

steps.title: בן ננס: the פסוק says "to ה׳" too, so it means the sheep
steps.stepSummary: בן ננס points out that the פסוק says "to ה׳ for the כהן." That describes something split between the מזבח and the כהן, meaning the sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בן ננס? Does it say "holy for the כהן"? It says "holy to ה׳ for the כהן"! Which item is partly for ה׳ and partly for the כהן? The sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how בן ננס would reject רבי עקיבא's reading. He says the words "to ה׳" cannot be ignored.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק meant only the כהן, it would just say "for the כהן." Since it also says "to ה׳," the item must be shared. The two sheep are שלמים: part is burned on the מזבח and part is eaten by the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: is it written…? (a rhetorical challenge)
that part of it
sheep (here, the two sheep of שלמים)

phrases.english: And ben Nannas?
Is it written: "They shall be holy for the priest"?!
"They shall be holy to the Lord for the priest" is written!
Which item is partly for the Lord
and partly for the priest?
You must say: these are the sheep.
phrases.notes: These are the two sheep brought as שלמים; some parts go on the מזבח and the rest is eaten by the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֶן נַנָּס מִי כְּתִיב ״קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיוּ לַכֹּהֵן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives בן ננס's opposing reading of the same פסוק
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבי עקיבא's reading that the פסוק describes something wholly for the כהן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It ignores the words "to ה׳," which point to a shared item, the sheep

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: ה׳ acquires it and gives all of it to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the פסוק doesn't say "to ה׳ AND to the כהן." It means ה׳ takes ownership and then hands the whole item to the כהן, as רב הונא says.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? Does it say "to ה׳ and to the כהן"? It says "to ה׳ for the כהן," like רב הונא said: ה׳ acquired it and gave it to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי עקיבא defends his reading. The missing word "and" shows the item is not split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without "and," the פסוק is not describing two separate owners. It describes one chain: first it belongs to ה׳, then ה׳ gives it fully to the כהן. That fits the bread, which goes entirely to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: "and to the כהן": the word "and" that is missing from the פסוק
ה׳ acquired it
and gave it to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: "לה׳ לכהן" does not mean half for ה׳ and half for the כהן according to רבי עקיבא. It means it goes to ה׳ first, and then all of it goes to the כהן.
steps.whatToRemember: Second explanation: בן ננס reads "לה׳ לכהן" as shared, so it means the sheep. רבי עקיבא reads it as ה׳ giving everything to the כהן, so it means the bread.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
Is it written: "They shall be holy to the Lord and to the priest"?
phrases.notes: The point is the word "and." It isn't in the פסוק, so the item isn't split between two owners.

phrases.english: "To the Lord for the priest" is written,
in line with Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said:
God acquired it and gave it to the priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִי כְּתִיב ״קֹדֶשׁ יִהְיוּ לַה׳ וְלַכֹּהֵן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי עקיבא against בן ננס's reading in Step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the wording (no "and") plus support from רב הונא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "לה׳ לכהן" means part for ה׳ and part for the כהן (the sheep)
steps.terutzMaskana: It means ה׳ acquires it and gives it entirely to the כהן (the bread)

steps.title: רבי יוחנן opens with a point everyone agrees on
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן begins a new statement about the משנה's argument, saying that on a certain point all opinions agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Everyone agrees...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new statement from רבי יוחנן. These words are only the opening, and the actual point of agreement comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא focused on where רבי עקיבא and בן ננס disagree: whether the sheep hold back the bread or the bread holds back the sheep. Now רבי יוחנן changes direction and points to something both of them accept. The words 'everyone agrees' tell us their argument has limits.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees. It marks a point that all opinions accept, even people who argue elsewhere.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי יוחנן is siding with רבי עקיבא or with בן ננס. 'Everyone' means both of them, so he is pointing to common ground and not choosing a side.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
Everyone concedes

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the פסוק-based debate in steps 25–29 to a new אמורא statement setting out common ground in the משנה's argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of רבי יוחנן's statement: there is a point on which רבי עקיבא and בן ננס both agree. The content follows.
